title: The boxes · Box 4B
logline: The editor's visit, as the brief has it: a strip. The one gridded page in the private work, because the conversation wanted the form.

margin.note: ROFLCOPTER — and under it, once: A. Finch.

panels.composition: The garage. THE EDITOR, late twenties, dark green coat, tote, notebook, standing among the banker's boxes — forty of them, numbered — looking up at the stacks. WOOD at the table, drawn from the front, plainly, for the first time in six years. BARNABY II.

characters.pose: at the table, from the front

balloons.text: Where is the unreleased graphic novel? The epic timber allegory everyone on the forums talked about?

image.prompt: a young woman in a dark green coat with a tote bag and notebook standing among forty numbered cardboard banker's boxes stacked in a garage studio looking up at them, a man in his mid-forties in a plaid flannel at a drafting table facing the viewer plainly, a three-legged dog, a four-panel grid returning to an otherwise borderless body of work, spare ink and ochre watercolor
image.notes: Wood from the front, plainly. The grid returns for one page.

panels.composition: Wood pointing at a box holding down an uneven corner of the rug.

characters.pose: pointing at a box on the rug

balloons.text: Box 4B. Sixty pages of pretentious garbage drawn between 2001 and 2003. It's mostly unreadable.

image.prompt: a man pointing at a cardboard box labeled 4B that weighs down the uneven corner of a rug in a garage

panels.composition: The editor, looking at the wall of strips, then at him.

balloons.text: So... you wasted thirty years drawing a daily newspaper strip about a small town?

image.prompt: a young woman looking from a wall covered in comic strips to the man who drew them, notebook lowered

panels.composition: Wood looking at the wall. The pup. The forty boxes. The editor with her hand already on box 21.

balloons.text: Ten thousand days of noticing things. Nothing gets wasted unless you weren't looking.

image.prompt: a wide garage panel: a man looking at a wall covered in decades of comic strips, a three-legged dog at his feet, a young woman with her hand resting on a box numbered 21 among forty numbered boxes, spare ink and watercolor
image.notes: Her hand on box 21: the private work, about to be found.

art.line: spare, knowing; economy of line; Era I's black spotting back on purpose in the mill run
art.palette: muted ochres, slate blues, misty sea-foam greens; luminous sunbreaks in the last spring
art.paper: Arches; bristol; the backs of motel registration cards

notes: The brief's Arc 5 daily, kept as a strip inside the private pages. Her hand on 21.
